summary: The checked legal facts are solid. Taiwan's 2019 idling regulation (under the Air Pollution Control Act) targets vehicles waiting over 3 minutes and exempts traffic-control idling, rain and hot days, so an ordinary red-light wait is not what it regulates; whether it reaches scooters is unresolved. MOTC marking rules let the two-stage turn box sit 50 cm from the crosswalk. The 2024 pedestrian act creates vehicle-controlled pedestrian zones but never mentions air. Health evidence supports careful claims only: Taipei walkers' traffic PM2.5 was associated with short-term rises in blood pressure, heart rate and an oxidative-stress marker (Chuang 2020); old, poorly maintained Taiwanese scooters emit many times more CO, hydrocarbons and VOC (Tsai 2017, 2026); scooters rank first per km for benzene but not for PM2.5. No source measures pedestrians' harm from idling scooter packs. Zones, hedges and trees show mixed, site-specific results. One numeric error (Xiao 2024 ORs) was corrected. Programme counts, polls, noise limits and scramble roll-out remain unverified.

findings.claim: Taiwan's 汽車停車怠速管理辦法 (Ministry of Environment; amended 2019-01-25) requires engines off when idling while stopped and waiting more than 3 minutes in car parks, on roads (excluding expressways) and in other parking/transfer places. Art. 4 exempts, among others, idling caused by traffic control, road congestion or accidents (item 5), days when the forecast maximum exceeds 30 C (item 6), and any time it is raining (item 7). Electric vehicles are excluded (art. 2).
findings.citation: 汽車停車怠速管理辦法, arts. 2-4, amended 民國108年1月25日, 全國法規資料庫
findings.quote: 汽車於下列場所，停車怠速等候逾三分鐘者，應關閉引擎 ... 因交通管制、道路壅塞或交通事故等致停車怠速於行駛道路中之汽車
findings.verifierNote: I fetched and read all 5 articles. Original claim correct but incomplete: it omitted the heat (>30 C) and rain exemptions, which together exempt most days in much of Taiwan. Art. 2 defines 汽車 as engine-driven road vehicles 'but excluding electric vehicles' with no explicit mention of motorcycles; the parent Act art. 3 includes motorcycles.
findings.caveats: Whether scooters are covered and whether a signal wait is 停車怠速等候 is interpretive; not resolved by any official interpretation I could open. Do not say red-light idling is legal or illegal.
findings.useOnSite: The rule is built for vehicles waiting more than 3 minutes and exempts traffic-control idling, heat and rain; an ordinary red-light wait is not what it targets.

findings.claim: Air Pollution Control Act art. 3 defines idling as a vehicle keeping its engine running while stopped and 汽車 as including motorcycles; art. 76 sets NT$1,500-60,000 for breaching the idling rules.
findings.citation: 空氣污染防制法 arts. 3, 38, 76, 全國法規資料庫
findings.quote: 汽車：指在道路上不依軌道或電力架設，而以原動機行駛之車輛，包括機車 / 處汽車使用人或所有人新臺幣一千五百元以上六萬元以下罰鍰
findings.verifierNote: Read live page; it displays 修正日期 民國107年8月1日 (2018-08-01) as of the Nov 2026 database snapshot, so the amendment date is confirmed as shown. Art. 38 is the delegation to the idling regulation.
findings.caveats: Practical enforcement against scooters not verified.
findings.useOnSite: The Act counts motorcycles as 汽車; coverage under the 2019 regulation is the open question.

findings.claim: The former fine schedule explicitly set NT$1,500 for 機器腳踏車 idling, escalating to NT$15,000; revoked 2019-08-19 (in force from 2012-03-01).
findings.citation: 違反機動車輛停車怠速管理規定罰鍰標準 (廢), 全國法規資料庫
findings.quote: 機器腳踏車：處新臺幣一千五百元；經令其改善而未改善者 ... 最高得至新臺幣一萬五千元
findings.verifierNote: Page shows 廢止日期 民國108年8月19日; art. 3 gives 民國101年3月1日 start. Note it was made under the old art. 63-1 and old art. 34-1 of the Act.
findings.caveats: Revoked; shows past intent only. Penalty counts not found.
findings.useOnSite: Taiwan once had an explicit motorcycle idling fine (2012-2019); no longer in force.

findings.claim: APCA art. 40 lets city and county authorities designate 空氣品質維護區 and restrict specific vehicles, fuels, power types or operating conditions; the city proposes and the central authority approves. Art. 76 para 2 sets the penalty for breaching a published zone measure: NT$500-60,000 for a 汽車 user or owner (and NT$5,000-1,000,000 for other mobile sources).
findings.citation: 空氣污染防制法 arts. 3(13), 40, 76, 全國法規資料庫
findings.quote: 各級主管機關得視空氣品質需求及污染特性，因地制宜劃設空氣品質維護區，實施移動污染源管制措施
findings.verifierNote: Power confirmed; added the penalty provision I read in art. 76 para 2. Actual zones, older-scooter rules and results still not verified.
findings.caveats: Legal power only.
findings.useOnSite: Cities already have the legal power to restrict higher-emitting vehicles in defined zones.

findings.claim: Art. 44: in-use 汽車 (incl. scooters) require periodic emission inspection; failing vehicles must be repaired within one month and re-tested. Art. 46: officers may use visual or remote-sensing screening and require repair and inspection; members of the public may report a vehicle, which must then be inspected. Art. 94: reporting and reward schemes are set by each city; reporter identity must be kept confidential. Art. 79: failing or skipping inspection NT$1,500-60,000; art. 80: skipping periodic inspection NT$500-15,000.
findings.citation: 空氣污染防制法 arts. 44, 46, 79, 80, 94, 全國法規資料庫
findings.quote: 人民得向各級主管機關檢舉使用中汽車排放空氣污染物情形，被檢舉之車輛經各級主管機關通知者，應於指定期限內至指定地點接受檢驗
findings.verifierNote: Original correct; I added remote sensing (art. 46), roadside spot checks (art. 45) and penalties (arts. 79-80). The reward-money wording sits in art. 94 (reward funding is explicitly described for facility reports; vehicle-report rewards are left to city rules).
findings.caveats: No inspection rates, report counts or reward amounts retrieved.
findings.useOnSite: Riders whose scooters fail must repair; anyone can report a smoky vehicle.

findings.claim: MOTC marking rules: art. 191 requires the two-stage turn box rear edge to be at least 50 cm from the crosswalk line, but allows adjustment where pedestrian safety is unaffected; the box is drawn in front of the stop line and, where a zebra crosswalk exists, in front of (beyond) the crosswalk. Art. 174-2: the 機慢車停等區 is 2.5-6 m deep, behind the stop line at signalised junctions on roads of 60 km/h or less, for scooters other than large heavy motorcycles. Art. 191 also contemplates early green for waiting scooters at T-junctions.
findings.value: gap >= 0.5 m; stop box depth 2.5-6 m; rule amended 2026-03-11
findings.citation: 道路交通標誌標線號誌設置規則 arts. 174-2, 191, 全國法規資料庫 (修正日期 民國115年3月11日)
findings.quote: 待轉區後緣應與行人穿越道線間隔五十公分以上。但不影響行人穿越安全時，得依實際情形酌予調整 / 縱深長度為二點五公尺至六公尺
findings.verifierNote: Article numbers, wording and amendment date confirmed. Clarification: the 50 cm is a minimum gap between box and crosswalk line, so a waiting scooter can sit about half a metre from where pedestrians cross.
findings.caveats: A minimum, not a typical value; rule says nothing about air quality. Real junctions vary.
findings.useOnSite: National design rules allow a waiting scooter box as close as 50 cm to the crosswalk.

findings.claim: 行人交通安全設施條例 was promulgated 2024-05-01. Art. 7: cities designate 行人友善區 around hospitals, schools, offices and transit hubs and control vehicle use there (speed limits, calming, timed pedestrian streets, 行人優先區); art. 5 requires an annual published implementation report; art. 10 links subsidies to annual assessment; arts. 11-12 set fines (NT$30,000-150,000 for obstructions; NT$5,000-25,000 for arcade floors). Art. 14: commencement date set by the Executive Yuan.
findings.citation: 行人交通安全設施條例, 全國法規資料庫
findings.quote: 直轄市、縣（市）主管機關應就醫療院所、學校、機關、大眾運輸場站等行人密集場所周邊，公告指定範圍為行人友善區 ... 並管制車輛使用行為
findings.verifierNote: Read all 14 articles. Original said 'annual publication of progress' — confirmed (art. 5). Small corrections: art. 7 also requires central authority filing and public briefings. The Act never mentions air quality or scramble phases.
findings.caveats: Commencement date not confirmed. Air-quality co-benefit is inference only.
findings.useOnSite: Since 2024 the law obliges cities to create vehicle-controlled pedestrian zones near schools and hospitals; it sets no air targets.

findings.claim: Taiwan's 機動車輛噪音管制標準 (amended 2020-12-01) sets acceleration and stationary noise limits in annex tables (phases 1-5 table 1, phase 6 table 2) and driving noise in table 3; in-use stationary checks may be done at roadsides.
findings.citation: 機動車輛噪音管制標準, 全國法規資料庫
findings.quote: 使用中車輛檢驗測定：指主管機關不定期於停車場（站）、路旁 ... 執行車輛噪音原地噪音檢驗測定
findings.verifierNote: Read body text and date; annexes not opened.
findings.caveats: No dB value for scooters read.
findings.useOnSite: Say only that a phased standard exists.

findings.claim: Two-stroke scooters, a small fraction of the fleet, can dominate urban vehicular pollution through organic aerosol and aromatic emission factors up to thousands of times higher; exhaust SOA also forms potentially toxic reactive oxygen species.
findings.value: up to thousands of times higher
findings.citation: Platt SM, El Haddad I, Pieber SM, et al. (2014) Nat Commun 5:3749
findings.quote: vehicles that constitute a small fraction of the fleet, but can dominate urban vehicular pollution through organic aerosol and aromatic emission factors up to thousands of times higher than from other vehicle classes
findings.verifierNote: Crossref: Nature Communications 5, article 3749, 2014-05-13, 22 authors; abstract read via OpenAlex.
findings.caveats: Two-stroke only, laboratory and chamber, not Taiwan, not pedestrians.
findings.useOnSite: Mechanism evidence for old two-stroke scooters only.

findings.claim: 40 four-stroke motorcycles on a dynamometer: CO ratios Phase IV/III 0.66 and V/III 0.42; HC 0.61 and 0.57; BTEX down 37-58% (IV) and 44-62% (V) vs Phase III; NOx highest in Phase V; emissions rise with age and mileage.
findings.citation: Tsai J-H, Yao Y-C, Huang P-H, Chiang H-L (2017) Aerosol Air Qual Res 17(5):1214-1223
findings.quote: BTEX decreased by 37-58% and 44-62%, respectively, for Phases IV and V motorcycles compared to those of Phase III
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read; Crossref confirms 4 authors, volume 17 issue 5 pp. 1214-1223. Total VOC of Phase V lowest at 0.59 g/km.
findings.caveats: ECE laboratory cycle, not intersection idling; PM not measured; NOx rose.
findings.useOnSite: Tighter standards cut CO, HC and benzene-family emissions; older high-mileage scooters emit more.

findings.claim: Taichung 2014 vs 2025 on-road and emission study: the 2025 driving cycle had a lower percentage of idling than 2014; in a case study of three motorcycles, Phase IV vs Phase VII ratios were 14.0 (CO) and 32.1 (HC); VOC 22-28 times and OFP 22-52 times higher for Phase IV; deteriorated Phase IV 'high-emitters' had CO 6.36-6.94%. Authors conclude engine technology and maintenance status governed emissions more than driving pattern, and call retirement of high-emitting legacy vehicles the most critical factor for ozone precursors.
findings.value: CO x14.0, HC x32.1, VOC x22-28, OFP x22-52
findings.citation: Tsai J-H, How V, He Z-J, Chan Y-H, Chiang H-L (2026) Results in Engineering 32:112353
findings.quote: Phase IV/Phase VII emission ratios reaching 14.0 for CO and 32.1 for HC
findings.verifierNote: Numbers confirmed in abstract (Crossref: vol 32, article 112353, dated 2026-12). Correction: the high ratios involve deteriorated 'IV-H' high-emitters among only three vehicles; the authors also say multiple urban factors affect the idling change.
findings.caveats: Three motorcycles; ozone precursors not pedestrian PM or health.
findings.useOnSite: Maintenance and retirement of high emitters matter more than driving style; idling share fell 2014 to 2025.

findings.claim: Taipei periodic inspection data 1996-2005: testing rate rose from about 50% to 70%, failure rate fell from about 15% to 10%; failure rose for scooters older than 3 years or beyond 10,000 km; two-stroke failure rates higher than four-stroke.
findings.citation: Chen Y-C, Chen L-Y, Jeng F-T (2009) J Air Waste Manag Assoc 59(6):757-762
findings.quote: the testing rate rose from approximately 50 to 70% and the failure rate changed from approximately 15 to 10%
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read; Crossref confirms 59(6):757-762, 3 authors.
findings.caveats: Data end 2005; Taipei only; 'rate' definitions as in paper.
findings.useOnSite: Historic Taipei inspection evidence; not current.

findings.claim: Taiwan road mobile-source inventory 2013-2021: four-stroke motorcycles were 32.6% of road activity (vehicle-km), second to gasoline cars at 42.6%; per-km PM2.5 and NOx ordering diesel > gasoline > motorcycle; HC motorcycle > gasoline; benzene motorcycle > gasoline >= diesel; formaldehyde diesel > motorcycle >= gasoline.
findings.value: 32.6% of vehicle-km; benzene order motorcycle > gasoline >= diesel
findings.citation: Tsai J-H, Chen J-Y, Chiang H-L (2023) Atmosphere 14(6):916
findings.quote: the emission sequence for benzene was motorcycle > gasoline ≥ diesel
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read. Corrected: PM2.5 factor from MOVES, NOx from MOBILE6.2, HC from gasoline-vehicle dynamometer data; benzene claim applies to emission factors, not totals.
findings.caveats: Modelled inventory per km, not roadside; scooters are not the top per-km PM2.5 or NOx source.
findings.useOnSite: Scooters stand out for hydrocarbons and benzene, not per-km particulates.

findings.claim: Fixed-site and mobile measurements at an urban intersection show PM varies through signal cycles and pedestrians face near-source PM both waiting at the roadside and crossing; cumulative deposited doses compared by journey segment.
findings.citation: He H-D, Gao HO (2021) Environ Pollut 268:115931
findings.quote: pedestrians are often at a higher risk of exposure to near-source PM pollution from traffic while waiting on the roadside or while walking in the crosswalk
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read; Crossref: Environmental Pollution 268, 115931, 2 authors, dated 2021-01. The abstract says 'often at a higher risk' as an introductory statement rather than a result, and gives no comparative numbers.
findings.caveats: Abstract only; not Taiwan; not scooter-specific; no waiting-vs-crossing number seen.
findings.useOnSite: Peer-reviewed intersection PM study; not scooter packs.

findings.claim: Interruption of steady traffic flow increases particle number emissions from motor vehicles (title only).
findings.citation: Jayaratne ER, Wang L, Heuff D, Morawska L, Ferreira L (2009) Transp Res D 14(7):521-526
findings.quote: Increase in particle number emissions from motor vehicles due to interruption of steady traffic flow
findings.verifierNote: Crossref confirms authors, journal, 14(7):521-526, October 2009. Abstract is publisher-elided on Semantic Scholar; I could not read it. Setting 'Brisbane, fleet' is unverified.
findings.caveats: Do not quote numbers.
findings.useOnSite: Pointer only.

findings.claim: 120 healthy Taipei adults, six commute modes, six repeated measurements 09:00-10:00 (also noise measured). PM2.5 highest in scooter mode (53.6 +/- 26.1 ug/m3), lowest on subway (21.7 +/- 5.8). Personal PM2.5 was associated with increased SBP (walking 6.5%, scooter 7.9%), HR (3.4%, 6.4%) and urinary 8-OHdG (8.1%, 8.9%). No significant effect on the subway; no significant PM2.5-BP/HR association when walking with a facemask.
findings.value: scooter 53.6 vs subway 21.7 ug/m3; walking SBP +6.5%, HR +3.4%, 8-OHdG +8.1%
findings.citation: Chuang K-J, Lin L-Y, Ho K-F, Su C-T (2020) Atmos Environ X 7:100084
findings.quote: personal exposure to PM2.5 was associated with increased SBP (W: 6.5%; Sc: 7.9%), HR (W: 3.4%; Sc: 6.4%) and urinary 8-OHdG (W: 8.1%; Sc: 8.9%)
findings.verifierNote: Numbers confirmed. Corrections: the scooter-mode figure is the rider's own exposure, not a pedestrian's; the mask null result is a notable fact; the paper recommends mass transit over scooters at rush hour. The abstract does not state the PM2.5 increment behind the percentages.
findings.caveats: Healthy adults, one morning hour; not red-light queues, children or elderly; traffic PM2.5 not source-split; short-term associations.
findings.useOnSite: Association between traffic PM2.5 while walking and short-term BP, heart-rate and oxidative-stress markers in healthy adults.

findings.claim: Hanoi pilot: mean BC on motorcycles 29.4 ug/m3 vs 10.1 on buses; peak traffic 34.7 vs 12.1; non-rush weekdays 27.7 vs 8.4.
findings.citation: Quang TN, Hue NT, Dat MV, Tran L, Phi TH, Morawska L, Thai PK (2021) Atmos Environ 245:118029
findings.quote: The mean BC concentration on motorcycles was 29.4 μg/m3 compared to 10.1 μg/m3 in the buses
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read via Semantic Scholar; Crossref confirms 7 authors, vol 245, 118029. Measured riders on motorcycles vs cabins of cars and buses.
findings.caveats: Riders not pedestrians; pilot.
findings.useOnSite: Riders in scooter-dense traffic had about three times the BC of bus passengers; not a pedestrian result.

findings.claim: Meta-analysis of 41 studies: ORs 1.05 (1.02-1.07) per 4 ug/m3 NO2, 1.03 (1.01-1.05) per 1 ug/m3 PM2.5, 1.08 (1.03-1.14) per 0.5e-5 m-1 BC.
findings.citation: Khreis H, Kelly C, Tate J, Parslow R, Lucas K, Nieuwenhuijsen M (2017) Environ Int 100:1-31
findings.quote: 1.05 (1.02, 1.07) per 4μg/m3 nitrogen dioxide (NO2), 1.03 (1.01, 1.05) per 1μg/m3 Particulate Matter <2.5μm
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read via Europe PMC. Abstract opens by stating the causal question is 'unresolved'.
findings.caveats: Long-term, mostly Europe and North America, association; not scooter-specific.
findings.useOnSite: Modest association with childhood asthma at higher long-term traffic pollution.

findings.claim: Microsensor panels: 55 subjects in Kaohsiung 2019-2020 (50 in Bandung 2018-2019). Kaohsiung 5-min mean PM2.5 14.9 +/- 11.2 ug/m3, max 467.4. Community factories and mosquito-coil burning were the two most important exposure sources (+10.1 and +9.82 ug/m3 PM2.5 in Taiwan); agricultural-waste and incense burning also important in Taiwan. HRV change -0.9% to -2.5% per 10 ug/m3 PM2.5 or PM1 (pooled both countries, except LF/HF ratio).
findings.value: max 467.4 ug/m3; mean 14.9; HRV -0.9 to -2.5% per 10 ug/m3
findings.citation: Lung S-CC, Tsou M-C, Cheng C-Y, Setyawati W (2025) J Expo Sci Environ Epidemiol 35(2):264-277 (online 2024-05-28)
findings.quote: Community factories and mosquito coil burning are the two most important exposure sources
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read via Europe PMC. Corrected: the HRV range is stated for both countries' analyses, not Taiwan alone; the abstract does not list traffic as a source, but does not say traffic was tested and excluded, so 'traffic was not a main source' is an over-reading. Online date 2024.
findings.caveats: Does not isolate scooters or red lights.
findings.useOnSite: Short PM peaks associated with small immediate HRV changes; sources found were varied.

findings.claim: Taiwan 2023, 58,181 scooter riders aged 65+ in police-reported collisions; 15-day cumulative PM2.5 at 31 ug/m3 gave rate ratio 2.357 (1.419-3.914); same-day exposure showed limited association; mean PM2.5 13.4 ug/m3.
findings.citation: Kao H-M, Lo Y-C, Li C-Y, et al. (2025) Injury Epidemiology 12(1):65
findings.quote: The highest risk estimate was observed for 15-day cumulative exposure at 31 µg/m³ (rate ratio = 2.357; 95% CI: 1.419-3.914)
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read. Crossref: article 65, 12 authors, dated 2025-10-01.
findings.caveats: Riders as victims of ambient PM2.5; ecological; single year.
findings.useOnSite: Not about pedestrians; do not use on the red-light page.

findings.claim: Kathmandu stated-preference survey: each extra second of waiting time raised odds of switching off by 5.1% (OR 1.051, 95% CI 1.046-1.057, p<0.001); uncertain waiting time was the most common deterrent.
findings.citation: Bhandari R, Lama A, Dhital NB (2024) J Environ Sci 10:54-62
findings.quote: with a 1-second increase in waiting time, the odds of motorcyclists idle-stopping their motorcycle engines increase by 5.1%
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read; Crossref confirms 10:54-62. Note: the stated-preference survey varies waiting time; countdown display effect is inferred by the authors.
findings.caveats: Stated intentions; Nepal; no Taiwanese evidence found.
findings.useOnSite: Evidence that longer known waits increase stated willingness to switch off; untested in Taiwan.

findings.claim: Systematic review: 16 studies (8 LEZ, 8 congestion-charging); reductions in some CVD subcategories in five of six LEZ studies; other outcomes less consistent.
findings.citation: Chamberlain RC, Fecht D, Davies B, Laverty AA (2023) Lancet Public Health 8(7):e559-e574
findings.quote: Current evidence suggests LEZs can reduce air pollution-related health outcomes, with the most consistent effect on cardiovascular disease
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read via Europe PMC.
findings.caveats: Car and van zones; no scooter content.
findings.useOnSite: Encouraging for heart outcomes; non-scooter.

findings.claim: German most-restrictive LEZ cut average fine PM by about 4% (up to 8% at the highest-polluting monitor) and exceedance days by three per year; reductions too small for substantial infant health improvement.
findings.citation: Gehrsitz M (2017) J Environ Econ Manage 83:121-144
findings.quote: these reductions are too small to translate into substantial improvements in infant health
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read via Semantic Scholar; Crossref confirms volume 83, pp. 121-144 (the researcher's missing page range is now resolved).
findings.caveats: Car and truck zones; infant outcomes.
findings.useOnSite: Cautionary precedent.

findings.claim: London LEZ (Feb 2008) vs 2,164 children aged 8-9, 2009-10 to 2013-14: share at addresses over NO2 limit fell 99% (444/450) to 34% (150/441); roadside NO2 -1.35 ug/m3/yr; PM10 no reduction, PM2.5 equivocal; FVC inversely correlated with NO2 (-0.0023 L per ug/m3) and PM10; no evidence of fewer children with small lungs.
findings.citation: Mudway IS, Dundas I, Wood HE, et al. (2019) Lancet Public Health 4(1):e28-e40
findings.quote: We found no evidence of a reduction in the proportion of children with small lungs over this period
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read in full. Correction: no PM10 reduction; the zone targeted heavy diesel.
findings.caveats: Cross-sectional; not scooter.
findings.useOnSite: Zones can lower NO2 near schools; lung benefit not shown.

findings.claim: One year after ULEZ (April 2019), London children (84 schools, 1,992 children aged 6-9) were more likely than Luton children to switch from inactive to active travel to school (OR 3.64, 95% CI 1.21-10.92) and less likely to switch active to inactive (OR 0.11, 0.05-0.24).
findings.citation: Xiao C, Scales J, Chavda J, et al. (2024) Int J Behav Nutr Phys Act 21:89
findings.quote: Relative to the children in Luton, children in London were more likely to have switched from inactive to active modes (OR 3.64, 95% CI 1.21-10.92)
findings.verifierNote: REFUTED NUMBERS: the original OR 3.51 (1.68-7.31) and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) do not appear in the abstract; the abstract gives 3.64 (1.21-10.92) and 0.11 (0.05-0.24). Citation corrected to volume 21, article 89 (2024-09-05); first author Xiao C confirmed via Crossref (27 authors). Switch rates: 42% London vs 20% Luton inactive-to-active.
findings.caveats: Travel mode self-reported on one day; no air-quality or health outcome; school-gate walking comparison only.
findings.useOnSite: London's ULEZ was followed by more active school travel; a travel result only.

findings.claim: UK playground 'tredge': western red cedar removed about 49% of BC, 46% of traffic-sourced PM2.5 and 26% of PM1; roadside vegetation can also increase PM by impeding airflow.
findings.citation: Maher BA, Gonet T, Karloukovski VV, et al. (2022) Sci Rep 12:14236
findings.quote: PM deposition on the western red cedar tredge removed ~ 49% of BC, and ~ 46% and 26% of the traffic-sourced PM2.5 and PM1, respectively
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read via OpenAlex; Crossref: Scientific Reports 12, article 14236, 2022-08-20.
findings.caveats: Single site; species-specific; playground not a signal queue.
findings.useOnSite: Promising, site-specific.

findings.claim: Łódź, Poland: PM2.5 and PM10 measured at 1.4 m on school routes in June 2022 (n = 242). Each one-percentage-point increase in vertical crown density corresponded to about 1.9% more PM at child height; higher leaf area index gave higher foliar PM retention. Trees may increase pedestrian exposure.
findings.value: +1.9% PM per percentage point of vertical crown density
findings.citation: Hoppa A, Sikorski P, Przybysz A, et al. (2026) Sci Rep 16:30792
findings.quote: each one percentage-point increase in vertical crown density corresponded to roughly 1.9% more PM at child height
findings.verifierNote: Upgraded from title-only: abstract now read. Setting is Łódź, Poland (researcher said unverified); Crossref: volume 16, article 30792, 2026-07-04.
findings.caveats: Cross-sectional, one month, Poland; association.
findings.useOnSite: Reason to word green-barrier claims cautiously: dense crowns can raise child-height PM.

findings.claim: Review: electric two-wheelers are generally more energy efficient and less polluting than conventional vehicles; 'tend to decrease exposure to pollution' as impacts arise mainly from production and electricity generation outside urban areas; large-scale adoption can reduce traffic noise and congestion; the authors call for case-specific assessment before concluding on sustainability.
findings.citation: Weiss M, Dekker P, Moro A, Scholz H, Patel MK (2015) Transp Res D 41:348-366
findings.quote: these are generally more energy efficient and less polluting than conventionally-powered motor vehicles
findings.verifierNote: Abstract read; Crossref confirms volume 41, pp. 348-366. The earlier 'highlights' quote is not in the abstract; use the abstract wording. The abstract also supports a noise statement (qualitative).
findings.caveats: Not a street-level before-after measurement; no Chinese-city air result found.
findings.useOnSite: Reviews find e-two-wheelers cleaner and quieter; direct street-air measurement not retrieved.

findings.claim: WHO Europe 2018 Environmental Noise Guidelines: recommendations on road traffic, rail, aircraft, wind turbine and leisure noise; levels can be considered applicable in other regions.
findings.citation: WHO Regional Office for Europe (2018) Environmental noise guidelines for the European Region, ISBN 9789289053563
findings.quote: the recommended exposure levels can be considered applicable in other regions and suitable for a global audience
findings.verifierNote: I did not re-open the WHO page in this check; web search budget was exhausted and I did not repeat the researcher's fetch. Not independently confirmed.
findings.caveats: No dB values.
findings.useOnSite: Do not print dB values until read from the full guideline.

doNotClaim: Do not say scooters at a red light are breaking Taiwan's idling law; the rule targets waits over 3 minutes, exempts traffic-control idling, rain and days above 30 C, and its coverage of scooters is unresolved.
Do not say any study measured pedestrian exposure or health harm specifically from scooter packs idling at red lights; none was found.
Do not call scooters Taiwan's largest source of fine particles; Tsai 2023 ranks motorcycles below diesel and gasoline per km for PM2.5 and NOx.
Do not apply two-stroke findings (Platt 2014) to the current four-stroke fleet.
Do not present Chuang 2020 effects as caused by scooter exhaust at junctions, or the scooter-mode PM2.5 as a pedestrian figure.
Do not claim the Pedestrian Traffic Safety Facilities Act, scramble phases or setbacks have measured air-quality benefits.
Do not claim LEZs or electrification improved pedestrian health in Taiwan.
Do not quote child asthma ORs as the effect of one red light.
Do not print WHO noise dB values or Taiwanese scooter dB limits.
Do not quote figures for Jayaratne 2009.
Do not use the Xiao 2024 ORs 3.51 or 0.22; the abstract says 3.64 and 0.11.
Do not say Lung 2025 shows traffic was not a source in Kaohsiung; the abstract only names other sources.
Do not use the 'Brisbane' setting for Jayaratne 2009 or present the ULEZ result as an air-quality outcome.
gaps: Web search budget was exhausted during this check, so none of these gaps could be closed: two-stroke retirement counts and subsidies; current 定檢 and 烏賊車 report statistics and rewards; actual 空氣品質維護區 zones; 紅燈熄火 campaigns; scramble phase and setback roll-out counts; polls and complaint counts; scooter dB limits (annex tables not opened) and roadside noise; WHO road-traffic Lden/Lnight values; measured street-level effects of Chinese e-two-wheeler transition.
No Taiwanese study of pedestrian exposure at scooter-filled red lights found.
Jayaratne 2009 abstract unread; WHO noise page not re-opened.
Pedestrian Traffic Safety Facilities Act commencement date unconfirmed.
